description:
Data Engineer
 Job Family : 
Data Science & Analysis Travel Required : 
Up to 10% Clearance Required : 
Ability to Obtain Public Trust 
 
 What You Will Do : 
 Guidehouse seeks a Data Engineer I to support the development, maintenance, and enhancement of data pipelines, cloud-based data platforms, and analytics solutions. The ideal candidate is an early-career professional with foundational experience in data engineering, software development, or cloud technologies who is eager to learn and grow in a collaborative environment.
 Assist in developing, testing, and maintaining data pipelines and ETL/ELT processes that ingest, transform, and load data from various sources.

 Support the implementation and enhancement of data models, databases, and cloud-based data solutions.

 Participate in data integration, migration, and modernization initiatives under the guidance of senior engineers.

 Develop and maintain scripts, queries, and applications using technologies such as Python, SQL, and PySpark.

 Support cloud-based data environments and services in AWS and Azure.

 Assist with the implementation of CI/CD processes and software development best practices using Git and related tools.

 Monitor data pipelines and systems, identify issues, and support troubleshooting and resolution activities.

 Perform data validation and quality assurance activities to help ensure data accuracy, completeness, and reliability.

 Collaborate with data engineers, developers, analysts, and other stakeholders to deliver high-quality solutions.

 Document technical processes, data flows, and system configurations.

 Continuously develop technical skills and stay current with emerging data engineering technologies and best practices.

 What You Will Need : 
 Must be able to OBTAIN and MAINTAIN a Federal or DHS PUBLIC TRUST.

 Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related technical field.

 Experience in data engineering, software engineering, data analytics, computer science, or a STEM related technical discipline.

 Foundational knowledge of programming languages such as Python, Java, or SQL.

 Basic understanding of relational databases and data querying concepts.

 Familiarity with cloud platforms such as AWS or Azure through coursework, certifications, internships, or professional experience.

 Exposure to data integration, ETL, data warehousing, or analytics concepts.

 What Would Be Nice To Have : 

 Internship, academic, research, or project experience involving data engineering, cloud computing, or software development.

 Exposure to Databricks, Spark, or large-scale data processing technologies.

 Familiarity with version control systems such as Git.

 Basic understanding of software development lifecycle and Agile methodologies.

 Strong analytical, problem-solving, and troubleshooting skills.

 Ability to learn new technologies and work collaboratively in a team environment.

 Strong verbal and written communication skills.

 Familiarity with AWS services such as S3, Lambda, or Redshift, or Azure services such as Azure Data Factory, Azure Functions, or Cosmos DB.

 Experience with data visualization or reporting tools such as Power BI, Tableau, or Kibana.

 Exposure to CI/CD tools and DevOps practices.

 AWS, Azure, Databricks, or related cloud/data certifications.

 Experience supporting healthcare, public sector, or federal clients.

 Interest in data architecture, machine learning, artificial intelligence, or advanced analytics.

 Previous consulting, client-facing, internship, or cooperative education experience.

The annual salary range for this position is $53,000.00-$88,000.00. Compensation decisions depend on a wide range of factors, including but not limited to skill sets, experience and training, security clearances, licensure and certifications, and other business and organizational needs.
